```{r}
#| results: asis
if (identical(params$lane, "start_portfolio")) {
  cat("## Question\n\nCan two sample-only producers supply reproducible starts for a broader three-factor CFA, and what do native versus mixed units cost?\n\n")
  cat("## Short answer\n\nAll four stock ULS fits returned finite admissible endpoints with exact start provenance. Both native-unit endpoints passed the default and verified Newton checks; both mixed-unit endpoints failed. Layered reduced the mixed-unit Newton distance from 2.14 to 0.85, still above the unchanged 0.01 budget. This paired pilot establishes construction/provenance feasibility, not reliability or default adoption.\n\n## Evidence\n\n")
  root <- "results/start-portfolio-pilot-v1"
  if(!file.exists(file.path(root,"observations.csv"))) stop("Run Rscript run_experiment.R --start-portfolio-pilot under timeout 180s")
  d <- read.csv(file.path(root,"observations.csv"))
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(Units=d$unit,Start=d$arm,Default=d$default_converged,
    Verified=d$verified_status,Objective=signif(d$objective,7),Distance=signif(d$distance,4),
    `Fit seconds`=d$fit_seconds,`Audit seconds`=d$audit_seconds),check.names=FALSE))
  cat("\nConstruction was below the process timer's resolution (recorded as zero); the four-fit serial runner took 0.34 seconds, including 0.304 seconds of fitting. Corrected separate endpoint audits took 0.054 seconds. The original boxed audit calls were unsupported; they remain saved locally, and no endpoint was refitted. The final runner requests unbounded geometry only for the separate audit, preserving the actual fit defaults.\n\n")
  cat("## Caveats\n\nExactly one n=200 Gaussian draw (seed 202610071) was used twice: unchanged and with indicator multipliers (1, 0.1, 10) repeated per factor. Covariances are centered with denominator $n$. The CFA has three factors, three indicators each, marker loadings one, other population loadings 0.8/0.6, latent variances one/correlations 0.25 and residual variances 0.6. ULS targets retain their original units; objectives across unit transforms are not directly comparable. Native FABIN3 and layered vectors were constructed for both inputs before any fit; there were no duplicate vectors, fallbacks, notes, warnings or errors. All primitive endpoint variances were positive and both primitive covariance matrices were PSD. Optimizer status was converged for all four, but this did not override failed mixed-unit convergence audits. Structural identification is not verified by this pre-TASK-33.3 runtime. No qualified endpoint exists for the mixed input.\n\n")
  cat("Compact observations, producer attributes, timing, metadata and summary are frozen for this bounded diagnostic; raw arrays, starts, inputs, audits and per-attempt records remain ignored. Input CSV hashes and source fingerprint are in metadata.\n\n## Reproduce\n\n```sh\nR_LIBS=~/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-e OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 timeout 180s Rscript run_experiment.R --start-portfolio-pilot\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:start_portfolio\n```\n\nRun inside the shared magmaan-work.slice through lane-start. The fixed run ID refuses overwrite; preserve existing evidence before reproducing in a fresh checkout.\n")
  cat("\n## Higher-order paired pilot\n\nThe two prespecified higher-order draws confirm exact FABIN3/default and layered start provenance across all eight attempts. Four native endpoints passed; no mixed endpoint qualified. Three mixed fits stopped with line-search failure and nonpositive audit curvature. The remaining mixed layered fit (seed 202610072) had Newton distance 0.0737, above the unchanged 0.01 budget, and a negative primitive variance (-1.22), with a covariance-admissibility warning. Thus layered supplied starts successfully but did not remove mixed-unit failures. Neither native arm lost an audit pass against the other; mixed arms both failed on both draws.\n\n")
  hroot <- "results/start-portfolio-higher-order-pilot-v1"
  h <- read.csv(file.path(hroot,"observations.csv"))
  print(knitr::kable(data.frame(Input=h$unit,Start=h$arm,Default=h$default_converged,
    Verified=h$verified_status,Objective=signif(h$objective,7),Distance=signif(h$distance,4),
    `Minimum variance`=signif(h$primitive_variance_min,4)),check.names=FALSE))
  cat("\nConstruction took 0.001 seconds, fitting 0.352 seconds, endpoint audits 0.080 seconds, and the complete serial runner 0.504 seconds. These short timings include timer resolution and first-call overhead; they establish cost for this pilot only. Seeds 202610072/073 each generated one n=200 Gaussian draw, paired with the same mixed-unit multipliers. Population higher loadings are (1, 0.8, 0.6), higher-factor variance 0.5, independent first-order residual variances 0.5, and indicator residual variances 0.6. Measurement loadings remain (1, 0.8, 0.6); first-order residual covariances are fixed at zero. Exact model/population/input fingerprints are frozen in metadata; full matrices and endpoints remain local. All eight objectives were consistent and all vectors distinct, without producer fallbacks. Structural identification remains unverified by this runtime. Cross-unit objectives are incomparable. This is timing/provenance evidence, not held-out reliability or adoption evidence.\n\nThe smallest proposed next step is an endpoint-only handoff of these four mixed failures to the shared optimizer work, with zero new fits; the owner can price any further diagnostic. No broader run or default change is justified by this pilot.\n\n```sh\nR_LIBS=~/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-e OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 timeout 180s Rscript run_experiment.R --start-portfolio-higher-order-pilot\n```\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
} else if (identical(params$lane, "port_nls")) {
  read_port <- function(run, file="comparisons.csv") {
    path <- file.path("results",run,file)
    if(!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing endpoint evidence: ",path,"; run --port-nls-witnesses with --probe")
    read.csv(path)
  }
  comparisons <- read_port(params$port_nls_run)
  fresh <- read_port(params$port_nls_fresh)
  regression <- read_port(params$port_regression)
  scalar <- rbind(read_port(params$port_nls_run,"scalar_checks.csv"),
                  read_port(params$port_nls_fresh,"scalar_checks.csv"))
  cat("\n## PORT endpoint consistency (TASK-33.7)\n\n",
    "**Question.** Can the adapter return matching coordinates and objectives\n",
    "at profiled PORT stops without changing convergence rules?\n\n",
    "**Short answer.** The adapter now recomputes the objective at the returned\n",
    "point and retains the best evaluated point when it is better by more than\n",
    "$10^{-14}$ relative. The raw stop code, stored backend value, backend\n",
    "returned-point value and substitution flag remain separate telemetry.\n",
    "The existing audit evaluates the selected endpoint.\n\n",sep="")
  cat(sprintf("All %d retained witnesses have reported and original expanded ULS objectives agreeing within $10^{-12}$ relative (maximum gap %.3g relative to $1+|f|$). All %d have no loss against the backend historical value. The %d fresh fits retain %d consistent endpoints, %d objective losses and %d audit losses. The six healthy ULS/GLS/WLS PORT and PORT-NLS controls retain bit-identical estimates in %d cases.\n\n",
    nrow(comparisons),max(comparisons$relative_original_gap),sum(comparisons$no_historical_loss),
    nrow(fresh),sum(fresh$consistent),sum(fresh$objective_loss),sum(fresh$audit_loss),sum(regression$estimate_bit_identical)))
  cat(sprintf("The common original-coordinate audit still fails all %d retained and %d fresh endpoints; recovery promotes no audit verdict. Ten unchanged fresh endpoints retain bit-identical estimates. These endpoint checks establish consistency, not successful minimization.\n\n",sum(comparisons$after_audit=="failed"),sum(fresh$after_audit=="failed")))
  cat("**Evidence.** The earlier `port-nls-endpoint-replay-final/comparisons.csv`\n",
    "preserves the 38 original failures: profiles and original objectives\n",
    "agreed at the returned coordinates while stored V(F) belonged to an earlier\n",
    "evaluation. The repair CSV preserves each before/after objective, normal\n",
    "audit verdict, raw stop and independent covariance/affine/profile checks.\n\n",sep="")
  print(knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(comparisons$before_audit,comparisons$after_audit)),
    col.names=c("Before audit","After audit","Retained witnesses")))
  cat(sprintf("\nScalar PORT has the same failure in both bounded `drmngb` and unbounded `drmng`: %d of %d baseline endpoints had a stored/returned-point discrepancy above $10^{-12}$ relative. After repair, %d of %d endpoints agree with independent original-objective recomputation. All %d previously exactly matching endpoints retain bit-identical nonlinear coordinates in %d cases.\n\n",
    sum(abs(scalar$before_reported-scalar$before_recomputed)>1e-12*(1+abs(scalar$before_recomputed))),nrow(scalar),sum(scalar$objective_consistent),nrow(scalar),sum(scalar$before_consistent),sum(scalar$before_consistent & scalar$estimate_bit_identical)))
  cat("**Caveats.** Consistency repairs the endpoint contract; it does not establish\n",
    "a trustworthy optimum or choose a new default. Singular/noisy raw stops\n",
    "survive recovery. All failed and unresolved audit outcomes remain in the\n",
    "CSV evidence. The 12 fixed-seed fresh fits are bounded confirmation within\n",
    "the two-factor study, not a general basin-success claim. No tolerance,\n",
    "stopping control, verdict rule or default changed.\n\n",
    "**Reproduce.** Build the optimized core and lane R package, then compile the\n",
    "diagnostic leaf against that core (use its Eigen include directory):\n\n",
    "```{.bash}\n",
    "eigen_include=/home/jonas/Files/research/magmaan/cpp/build-previous/fast/_deps/eigen3-src\n",
    "nice -n 10 clang++ -O3 -march=native -std=c++23 -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti \\\n",
    "  -DMAGMAAN_WITH_PORT -DEIGEN_NO_EXCEPTIONS -DEIGEN_MAX_ALIGN_BYTES=64 \\\n",
    "  -Icpp/include -I\"$eigen_include\" \\\n",
    "  experiments/engineering/active/15-sphere-reference-fits/scripts/profile_port_nls.cpp \\\n",
    "  cpp/build/opt/libmagmaan.a cpp/build/opt/_deps/nlopt-build/libnlopt.a \\\n",
    "  cpp/build/opt/libquadpack.a cpp/build/opt/libport.a -lm -o /tmp/profile_port_nls\n",
    "export OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1\n",
    "export R_LIBS=\"$HOME/.cache/magmaan-rlib/lane-a\"\n",
    "nice -n 10 Rscript experiments/engineering/active/15-sphere-reference-fits/run_experiment.R \\\n",
    "  --ordinary --port-nls-witnesses --run-id port-nls-endpoint-repair-v1 --probe /tmp/profile_port_nls\n",
    "nice -n 10 Rscript experiments/engineering/active/15-sphere-reference-fits/run_experiment.R \\\n",
    "  --ordinary --port-nls-witnesses --fresh --run-id port-nls-endpoint-fresh-v1 \\\n",
    "  --before-run port-nls-fresh-before --probe /tmp/profile_port_nls\n",
    "```\n\n",
    "Choose fresh run IDs; `--smoke` selects one witness per start/coordinate pair.\n",
    "Before/after estimate checks need the ignored baseline RDSs. Reproduce those\n",
    "with core commit `7f1025ca` and the same fixed-seed runner before installing\n",
    "the repaired package. `scripts/port_regression_controls.R RUN_ID BEFORE_RUN_ID`\n",
    "compares the six healthy controls. Frozen scalar baseline coordinates and\n",
    "objectives are in `port-scalar-before/points.csv`, with provenance alongside.\n",
    "The probe's `scalar` and `unbounded` modes measure the same profile problems. Raw\n",
    "inputs and fits remain ignored; the parent never reruns the 2400-fit grid.\n",sep="")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
if (identical(params$lane, "optimizer_audit")) {
  read_optimizer <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path("results",params$optimizer_run,paste0(name,".csv"))
    if(!file.exists(path))stop("Missing optimizer evidence: ",path,"; run --ordinary --optimizer-audit")
    read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }
  checks <- read_optimizer("verification")
  if(anyNA(checks$passed)||!all(checks$passed))stop("Optimizer mechanism verification failed")
  fits <- read_optimizer("fits")
  pinned <- fits[fits$expected=="pass",]
  early <- fits[fits$expected=="failed_candidate",]
  retained <- fits[fits$expected=="retained_candidate",]
  defaults <- fits[fits$expected=="observe",]
  cat("## Question\n\nDo equality constraints that pin a loading block produce the same start and fitted optimum as explicit constants, and can failed optimizer endpoints remain available for an independent audit?\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("## Short answer\n\nTwo shared defects are repaired. Layered starts now treat fully pinned parameters as constants during measurement and scale construction. All %d paired equality/fixed fits converge and match the independently fitted lavaan objective, including Little Table 10.3 corpus data and fresh draws at three scales. Finite NLopt budget and line-search exits now preserve their candidates, raw stop codes and actual adapter controls. All %d deliberate early stops return candidates and fail the numerical verdict.\n\n",nrow(pinned),nrow(early)))
  summary <- data.frame(Scope=c("Pinned equality and explicit fixed models","Deliberate evaluation stops","Ordinary default route controls","Retained mixed-unit ML2S fits"),
    Attempts=c(nrow(pinned),nrow(early),nrow(defaults),nrow(retained)),
    Returned=c(sum(pinned$returned),sum(early$returned),sum(defaults$returned),sum(retained$returned)),
    Passed=c(sum(pinned$fit_passed,na.rm=TRUE),sum(early$fit_passed,na.rm=TRUE),sum(defaults$fit_passed,na.rm=TRUE),sum(retained$fit_passed,na.rm=TRUE)))
  print(knitr::kable(summary))
  cat(sprintf("\nThe largest paired-reference objective gap is %.2g. A separate determinant/trace calculation checks the original complete-data ML objective at every paired endpoint. The early-stop checks cover ML, ULS, DWLS, WLS, direct FIML and all-ordinal DWLS, preserving a one-evaluation budget and explicit objective/step controls. The explicit FIML L-BFGS/SLSQP policy runs two stages and now counts both.\n\n",max(pinned$objective_gap)))
  oracle <- read_optimizer("oracle_controls")
  cat("The reference is fitted in known uniform data units, then its means/covariance are transported back and checked against the original likelihood. Fixed unit loadings and homogeneous mean constraints describe the same model under this transformation. Raw-unit lavaan attempts are also retained. In the preserved v3 confirmation, raw-unit lavaan stopped about 0.000222 above both native backends on one scale-100 draw; independently normalizing that reference closes the gap below $1.2\\times10^{-13}$. The original failed comparison gate remains frozen. This changes reference controls, not the native fit or comparison tolerance.\n\n")
  oracle_summary <- do.call(rbind,lapply(split(oracle,oracle$scale),function(z)
    data.frame(`Unit multiplier`=z$scale[1],References=nrow(z),
      `Largest raw-reference gap`=max(abs(z$raw_fmin-z$reference_fmin)),
      `Largest transported-likelihood gap`=max(abs(z$transported_objective-z$reference_fmin)),
      check.names=FALSE)))
  print(knitr::kable(oracle_summary,digits=10,row.names=FALSE))
  cat("\nEarlier confirmations also exposed an R ownership defect during serialization and expensive automatic inference at a rejected ML2S endpoint. Sample-mean lists now remain protected across allocations; automatic ML2S inference requires the C++ fit verdict to pass. Failed fits still own the stage inputs needed for explicit audits. The crash, terminated tail calculation and failed reference comparison are retained in the execution register and partial/full attempt CSVs. Noncentral chi-square tail cost remains a separate follow-up.\n\n")
  metadata <- read_optimizer("metadata")
  cat(sprintf("\nThe complete final run took %.2f seconds; summed native fit-call time was %.2f seconds, including existing post-fit work. Per-attempt function/gradient counts, all NLopt adapter fields and oracle iterations are retained. These sequential timings do not rank fitting engines.\n\n",as.numeric(metadata$value[metadata$key=="seconds"]),sum(fits$seconds)))
  cat("## What the repair explains\n\nOn the retained Little corpus data, the equality formulation previously constructed latent starting variances around $10^{14}$ and stopped at an objective above 124, while its explicitly fixed equivalent converged at about 0.7142. The constraint reduction already described the correct feasible model; recognizing its fully pinned rows before measurement/scale construction repairs the start. The corpus result corresponds to chi-square about 537.10; it is a reconstructed witness of the reported mechanism, not a replay of the supplement's particular draw with chi-square 271.\n\n")
  cat("The scalar variance domain probe still exposes the generic L-BFGS limitation: variances 1 and 0.01 solve, but variance $10^{-6}$ aborts after 12 evaluations from ten times its optimum, despite a budget of 5,000. Expressing that same scalar objective in variance units solves the diagnostic example. The adapter adds no retry, finite penalty, longer line search or new optimizer default. Candidate retention makes the failure reviewable; it does not recover it.\n\n")
  if(nrow(retained)) {
    losses <- retained[!is.na(retained$fit_passed)&!retained$fit_passed,]
    cat(sprintf("All %d mixed-unit ML2S attempts now return endpoints; %d remain rejected. The NT and DLS comparisons use the same Stage-1 inputs. Separate owning Stage-1/handoff/Stage-2 audits are retained, so backend telemetry cannot supply a composite pass.\n\n",nrow(retained),nrow(losses)))
  }
  cat("## Scope and next work\n\nThis banks a start-construction repair and finite NLopt candidate retention. It leaves safeguarded domain recovery, complete fallback histories, uniform backend telemetry and outer-loop stopping open on TASK-33.10.5. Identification, broader starts and numerical/default adoption keep their own cards. The local Newton budget $d\\leq0.01$ remains an explicit diagnostic, rather than a new production acceptance policy; there is no new propagated construction interval or inference/PSD claim. An existing explicit PSD fallback retains its prior original-start behavior after a nonstationary budget/domain stop.\n\nEvery confirmation attempt, loss, cost, caller-control check and independent objective comparison is retained in compact CSVs. Raw observations and fitted objects remain local. The focused native gate passed 201 cases (4,322 assertions); candidate/ownership R tests passed 35 expectations and the existing ML2S audit tests passed 20. Other completed report lanes remain selectable.\n\n")
  cat("## Reproduce\n\nUse matching isolated-worktree bindings and the optional textbook corpus; choose a fresh run ID.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --optimizer-audit --smoke --run-id optimizer-smoke-new\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --optimizer-audit --reps 2 --seed-base 865081601 --textbook-root /path/to/external/textbook-corpus --run-id optimizer-confirm-new\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:optimizer_audit -P optimizer_run:optimizer-confirm-new\n```\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
if (identical(params$lane, "ml2s_audit")) {
  read_ml2s <- function(run,name) {
    path <- file.path("results",run,paste0(name,".csv"))
    if(!file.exists(path))stop("Missing ML2S evidence: ",path,
      "; run --ordinary --ml2s-audit --run-id ",run)
    read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }
  gate <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"verification")
  if(any(gate$failed!=0))stop("ML2S verification failed; inspect its frozen checks")
  fits <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"fits")
  audits <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"audits")
  points <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"comparisons")
  handoffs <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"handoff_checks")
  producers <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"producer_checks")
  stages <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"stages")
  development <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_development,"fits")
  metadata <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"metadata")
  reference <- read_ml2s(params$ml2s_run,"reference_metadata")
  normal <- fits[fits$arm!="transformed_nt",]
  cat("## Question\n\nCan ML2S reuse the ordinary ML and weighted-LS numerical audits while separately verifying its saturated Stage-1 endpoint and the actual inputs handed to Stage 2?\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("## Short answer\n\nBank the conditional numerical composition. All %d fresh stage-point calculations, %d conditional producer checks and %d handoff checks agree with independent 90-digit calculations. All 12 ordinary Stage-1 endpoints pass. Of 60 ordinary fits, 54 return and pass the composed audit; six mixed-unit ULS/DWLS/ADF attempts end in L-BFGS errors without terminal candidates. Both additional transformed-NT controls return and pass.\n\n",nrow(points),nrow(producers),nrow(handoffs)))
  cat("A stage pass cannot replace missing or mismatched handoff evidence. Missing records and legacy solver evidence remain unchecked; wrong moments, mixing, weights and required ACOV fail. Early EM stops and a repaired-information point with negative raw curvature fail separately. This banks the numerical integration, while mixed-unit fitting recovery remains open. It supplies no propagated structural-parameter accuracy, inference recommendation or default change.\n\n")
  cat("## Evidence\n\n")
  evidence <- do.call(rbind,lapply(split(normal,normal$family),function(x) {
    result <- function(kind) {z <- x[x$kind==kind,];sprintf("%d/%d",sum(z$returned & z$fit_passed,na.rm=TRUE),nrow(z))}
    data.frame(Family=x$family[1],NT=result("nt"),ULS=result("uls"),DWLS=result("dwls"),ADF=result("adf"),DLS=result("dls"))
  }))
  cat(knitr::kable(evidence),sep="\n")
  cat("\n\nTwo fresh draws per family use means, a one-factor marker model, and the actual default L-BFGS starts/stopping options for each Stage-2 route. Stage 1 is built once with its public defaults and reused across weights. Unequal groups have 130 and 210 rows; shared loading labels exercise linear equalities. NT uses the original complete-data ML objective, not a quadratic approximation. DLS uses mixing 0.5. The additional complete/MCAR controls apply fixed diagonal covariance shrinkage of 0.25 and retain the original endpoint separately. These are engineering controls, not a regularization decision or an estimator-by-weight simulation programme.\n\n")
  cat("The six fresh errors are fits 44–46 and 49–51: ULS/DWLS/ADF on both mixed-unit draws. All reach an L-BFGS line-search failure after 12 iterations. Their Stage-1 objects exist and pass; no Stage-2 endpoint is manufactured. The development run also retains three such errors. These witnesses feed shared stopping/domain recovery (TASK-33.10.5), with starts and normalization kept explicit. There is no lost native pass among returned fits.\n\n")
  cat("Every returned fit has separate Stage-1, handoff, solver-stop and Stage-2 assessments. Twelve displaced Stage-2 points fail without changing their Stage-1 or handoff reports. Ten missing/mismatched/early/repaired controls return the required failed or unchecked result; a strict one-iteration EM call errors explicitly, while its opt-in last iterate retains the iteration-limit and covariance-repair history. That early-source control is evaluated with the original fit and recorded original handoff, so its Stage-2 report is a diagnostic evaluation rather than a newly fitted endpoint.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("Fitting and artifact collection took %.2f seconds; independent verification took %.1f seconds on one math thread. Summed Stage-1 build time was %.3f seconds and fit-call time %.3f seconds. The fit calls include their existing post-fit calculations; these short sequential timings do not rank fitting engines.\n\n",as.numeric(metadata$value[metadata$key=="elapsed_s"]),reference$elapsed_s,sum(stages$seconds),sum(fits$seconds)))
  cat("## What is verified\n\nStage 1 uses the actual raw observed-pattern normal likelihood. Its total gradient and observed Hessian are checked before any inversion safeguard. Literal per-row score outer products independently reconstruct $J$, and applicable ACOV checks use $(H+\\rho I)^{-1}J(H+\\rho I)^{-1}$ with the retained information-repair ridge $\\rho$. The fixed transformation is checked separately in both covariance and ACOV. The deliberately nonpositive-curvature controls' repaired ACOV remains unchecked; their raw curvature already rejects them, and repaired positive information never substitutes for that raw audit.\n\n")
  cat("Stage 2 retains exact means/covariances/counts, weight recipe, DLS mixing, required ACOV, supplied weights and bounds at fit time. The adapter checks this record against the source/transformation, the fit's caller-unit sample and the produced weight. The independent reference checks the same identities. A supplied record asserts historical input provenance; equality alone cannot reconstruct history for old fits. Serialized fits rebuild their packs and preserve owning reports.\n\n")
  cat("For NT, Stage-2 distance uses the observed likelihood Hessian. For fixed-weight LS, it uses the normal-theory variance of the total gradient, with the actual frozen fitting weight; observed objective curvature still has to be positive. These are separate conditional local distances. Adding them does not establish a numerical-error bound for the composed structural estimate.\n\n")
  cat("Native validation passes 72 cases/1783 assertions, including 17/17 FIML goldens and their applicable ML2S comparisons. The eight focused composition/adapter cases pass 197 assertions. Thin R tests pass 20 expectations, including bit-identical no-options versus cached-Stage-1 NT fitting, snapshot ownership, serialized auditing and failed/unchecked handoffs. The live R/lavaan FIML/ML2S example and bounded garbage-collection check also pass.\n\n")
  cat("## Caveats\n\nThe bank covers single-level joint continuous models with means, supported linear equalities, complete/MCAR/MAR inputs and unequal groups, conditional on actual Stage-1 and weight artifacts. Mixed-unit failures remain visible. The information repair can depend on units and is an existing inversion safeguard, not a statistical regularization choice justified here. There is no propagated construction interval or inference calibration; partial producer evidence cannot supply either. Identification remains a separate gate. Multilevel, missing fixed-x, active-bound/PSD-face/barrier geometry and broader search guarantees inherit no pass. The composed adapter rejects nonordinary covariance policies.\n\n")
  cat("An early pilot exposed an empty-artifact writer error for the missing-ACOV control. It was fixed before the fresh confirmation; no fitting or acceptance threshold was changed. Before confirmation, the independent ACOV check was also extended to positive raw-curvature endpoints whose inversion information had been repaired. Nonpositive raw-curvature controls keep their explicit unchecked repaired-ACOV limit.\n\n")
  cat("## Reproduce\n\nUse matching isolated-worktree bindings and Python with mpmath 1.3.0; use fresh run IDs. Compact point judgments, every fitting attempt, handoff/producer checks and provenance are frozen. Raw matrices, observations and serialized fits stay ignored. The earlier development summaries retain all three unit failures.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --ml2s-audit --smoke --run-id ml2s-smoke-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --ml2s-audit --reps 2 --seed-base 865071301 --run-id ml2s-confirm-new --python /path/to/python\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:ml2s_audit -P ml2s_run:ml2s-confirm-new\n```\n\nDevelopment inputs use seed 865071201 and one replicate. Shared backend/domain/stopping correctness (TASK-33.10.5) is the next integration card; identification, starts and audit-default adoption remain separate. Other report lanes remain selectable.\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}

All 16 actual-default fits pass, while standalone SLSQP passes 15/16, leaving one mixed-unit endpoint above budget. All eight deliberate early stops return errors without candidate artifacts.\n\n",nrow(points)))
  cat("This does not bank general fitting reliability. The earlier unit and weak-marker failures remain saved.   }))
  cat(knitr::kable(evidence),sep="\n")
  cat("\n\nEach family has two fresh draws. Both arms use identical actual public FABIN3 starts; no start tuning or polishing is added. The default uses L-BFGS with its existing SLSQP fallback. The shared 1000-evaluation budget and default tolerances remain fixed. PORT is rejected by this route. All returned fits, failures, backend counts and fit times are retained; these small engineering runs do not rank optimizers or select defaults.\n\n")
  loss <- points[points$target=="terminal" & points$arm=="slsqp" & points$passed=="FALSE",]
  cat(sprintf("The sole fresh SLSQP loss is fit %d, mixed-unit case %d, with observed-information Newton distance %.3f versus the native 0.01 budget. The paired default passes. The development replay retains one weak-marker default failure that SLSQP passes. None is discarded because the later draws are easier.\n\n",loss$fit_id,loss$case_id,as.numeric(loss$reference_distance)))
  cat("Actual raw rows independently reproduce every pattern selection, count, mean and divisor-N covariance, including singleton observations. Reversed named columns preserve the objective. Empty observed rows, nonfinite observed values and missing joint-observation pairs reject explicitly; the latter is a current pack-construction limit. Sparse-information and zero-loading saddle points reject, as does an invalid observed covariance. The focused native tests pass 71 cases/2016 assertions, including 17/17 FIML lavaan goldens; the live R/lavaan FIML example also passes. Serialized fits rebuild the pack, and returned artifacts remain valid after fit removal under a bounded garbage-collection stress check.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("The fresh fitting/artifact phase took %.2f seconds and the independent reference %.1f seconds with one math thread. Summed fit time was %.3f seconds across 40 attempts. These short sequential timings do not establish a speed ranking.\n\n",as.numeric(metadata$value[metadata$key=="elapsed_s"]),reference$elapsed_s,sum(fits$seconds)))
  cat("## Likelihood and audit convention\n\nFor each group-pattern $b$, let $n_b$ be its row count, $C_b$ its divisor-$n_b$ covariance, and $m_b=\\mu_{o_b}-\\bar x_b$. The evaluated per-row objective, omitting the normal constant, is\n\n$$f(\\theta)=\\frac{1}{2N}\\sum_b n_b\\{\\log|\\Sigma_{o_b o_b}|+\\operatorname{tr}(\\Sigma_{o_b o_b}^{-1}C_b)+m_b^\\top\\Sigma_{o_b o_b}^{-1}m_b\\}.$$\n\nThe independent reference rebuilds moments and their analytic first/second derivatives from the prepared model and exact binary64 inputs. Total-likelihood gradient and observed Hessian are reduced by the retained linear-equality basis. The conditional local distance is $\\sqrt{G^\\top H^{-1}G}$ when the reduced observed curvature is positive. This is a numerical endpoint check, not a sampling covariance or a calibrated inferential quantity. Complete-data ML differs by its accounted saturated-objective constant; gradients and observed curvature agree at the same points.\n\n")
  cat("Pairwise-complete statistics supply starts and existing information-coordinate preconditioning; they never replace the observed-pattern likelihood. Full raw-sample unit normalization is still separate work. This study checks the current unit handling rather than implementing a new normalization or numerical regularization.\n\n")
  cat("## Caveats\n\nThe bank covers conditional points and bounded ordinary fits for single-level joint normal models with means, linear shared loadings and unequal groups under complete, MCAR and MAR masks. It provides no propagated pattern-construction error interval; construction status remains `unsupported` at every point. Missing fixed-x, multilevel, nonlinear constraints, active bounds, sphere/PSD/barrier geometry and inference calibration inherit no pass. There is no global optimum or broad weak-data reliability claim.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("The scale-ridge control retains raw local pass = %s. Independently multiplying all factor loadings by 1.25 and dividing factor variance by $1.25^2$ preserves implied means/covariances to %.2g, and the moment Jacobian annihilates the corresponding scale direction. TASK-33.3 must supply a separate identification gate; this study implements no such guard. The original challenge's negative-control gate failed %d time and remains frozen. The final report scope explicitly excludes this proved unidentified model, without relabeling its raw local verdict.\n\n",ridge$raw_newton_passed,as.numeric(ridge$scale_invariance_error),sum(old_gate$failed)))
  cat("Before fresh confirmation, the independent reference was corrected to retain second derivatives at zero-loading saddles: zero first derivatives do not imply zero second derivatives. The corrected development replay agrees at all 37 points while preserving its failed fit. Fresh confirmation uses a new seed and the corrected frozen reference. Earlier failed checks remain local or frozen as described; no native audit tolerance or fitting setting was changed to obtain agreement.\n\n")
  cat("## Reproduce\n\nUse matching isolated-worktree bindings and Python with mpmath 1.3.0; choose fresh run IDs. Compact per-attempt judgments, reference checks and provenance are frozen to retain every failure and the earlier failed identification-control gate. Raw samples, full matrices and serialized fits remain ignored.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --fiml-audit --smoke --run-id fiml-smoke-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --fiml-audit --reps 2 --seed-base 865061401 --run-id fiml-confirm-new --python /path/to/python\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:fiml_audit -P fiml_run:fiml-confirm-new\n```\n\nRecreate the development and earlier challenge inputs with seed bases 865061201 (one replicate) and 865061301 (two), respectively. The retained-v2 bank is a reference-only replay of the development CSV inputs; its metadata preserves the original source fingerprints alongside the corrected reference fingerprint. Reopen integration for a pattern/moment/derivative mismatch, an unexplained local verdict within the declared scope, or a new domain/construction certificate. Next bank ML2S Stage-1/handoff composition; the concrete FIML start/stop and identification witnesses continue on their separate cards. Other report lanes remain selectable.\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}
if (identical(params$lane, "sparse_search")) {

  }
  fits <- read_sparse(params$sparse_run,"fits")
  cases <- read_sparse(params$sparse_run,"cases")
  retained <- read_sparse(params$sparse_retained,"fits")
  faces <- read_sparse(params$sparse_retained,"boundaries")
  replay <- read_sparse(params$sparse_retained,"replay_checks")
  points <- read_sparse(params$sparse_retained,"comparisons")
  fresh_points <- read_sparse(params$sparse_run,"comparisons")
  metadata <- read_sparse(params$sparse_run,"metadata")
  reference <- read_sparse(params$sparse_run,"reference_metadata")
  cat("## Question\n\nDo the six retained sparse-theta ULS/DWLS/WLS failures call for better starts or tighter optimization, or do they approach a boundary that finite theta parameters cannot represent?\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("## Short answer\n\nThe retained failures have a verified local boundary explanation. All six cold endpoints reproduce exactly. Three independent 90-digit face calculations show strict outward descent; finite theta paths approach the faces while remaining above the Newton budget. Tighter L-BFGS recovers none of the three weight-specific fits. All %d fits on the fresh controls pass and their independent point checks agree; two of the ten fresh sparse draws fail first-stage construction and remain recorded.\n\n",nrow(fits)))
  cat("Bank this as an explicit limit of the finite interior theta audit. No optimizer, start or audit default changes. The local evidence does not prove a global infimum or exclude a different finite basin.\n\n")
  cat("## Evidence\n\n")
  evidence <- do.call(rbind,lapply(split(fits,interaction(fits$family,fits$parameterization,drop=TRUE)),function(x) {
    result <- function(arm) {
      z <- x[x$arm==arm,];sprintf("%d/%d",sum(z$returned & z$fit_passed,na.rm=TRUE),nrow(z))
    }
    data.frame(Family=x$family[1],Parameterization=x$parameterization[1],Default=result("default"),PORT=result("port_nls"),`Tight L-BFGS`=result("tight_lbfgs"),check.names=FALSE)
  }))
  cat(knitr::kable(evidence),sep="\n")
  cat("\n\nThese are ten regular and ten sparse draws, with ULS/DWLS/WLS conditional on the same first-stage inputs. The two rejected sparse draws have singular polychoric score blocks; no fits are imputed for them. All returned fits are audited. There are no gains or losses among the three arms on these fresh controls. This small engineering comparison is not a default-selection study.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("The retained replay has %d agreeing independent points: 18 terminal points, 18 actual starts and 15 finite boundary-path points. All 12 stock delta/theta endpoints reproduce their original parameter vectors exactly; all three configurations receive identical actual starts. The six original theta failures and three tighter-control failures remain rejected. The earlier bank's saddle/rank controls retain their checks; this study changes only start telemetry at the R boundary.\n\n",nrow(points)))
  native <- metadata$value[metadata$key=="elapsed_s"]
  independent <- reference$elapsed_s[1]
  cat(sprintf("The fresh R phase took %.1f seconds and the independent reference %.1f seconds on one thread each. Summed fitting time was %.3f seconds across %d fits; median fit times were 3–4 ms. These short, sequential timings do not establish an optimizer speed ranking.\n\n",as.numeric(native),independent,sum(fits$seconds),nrow(fits)))
  cat("## Why these theta fits escape\n\nFor this single-factor model, positive factor variance $\\phi$ and unit theta residual variances give standardized loadings $c_j=\\lambda_j\\sqrt{\\phi}/\\sqrt{1+\\lambda_j^2\\phi}$, with $r_{ij}=c_ic_j$ and $|c_j|<1$ at every finite point. Thresholds can be eliminated exactly using the Schur complement of the retained fitting weight. The independent reduced objective then has only four loading coordinates.\n\n")
  cat("At the locally optimal face $c_1=1$, the other three loading derivatives vanish, their Hessian is positive, and the derivative toward larger $c_1$ is strictly negative for every weight. The finite path at factor variances from 100 to one million strictly lowers the original objective toward this face. The marker constraint fixes $\\lambda_1=1$; reaching the face therefore requires $\\phi\\to\\infty$.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("The delta fits instead have standardized x1 loadings of %.3f–%.3f and negative x1 residual variances. They cannot be transported into the positive-residual theta chart by finite real rescaling. Their convergence is a numerical result for an unrestricted objective, not evidence of an admissible fitted covariance decomposition.\n\n",min(faces$delta_max_abs_loading),max(faces$delta_max_abs_loading)))
  cat("## Caveats\n\nThis is a local face certificate in the positive-factor-variance chart, conditional on retained first-stage moments and weights. It supplies no global nonattainment theorem, first-stage error propagation, statistical regularization or inference recommendation. A boundary/PSD route needs its own constrained audit; the interior Newton audit must continue rejecting these finite endpoints.\n\n")
  cat("The development probe at factor variance $10^8$ is retained in `sparse-search-retained-v2`. Its ill-conditioned native ULS distance differs from the 90-digit value by 1.42e-8 relative, exceeding that probe's comparison tolerance; derivatives and the rejecting verdict still agree. The final native path comparison deliberately stops at $10^6$. That rejected diagnostic is not an accuracy certificate.\n\n")
  cat("PORT-NLS scalar objective telemetry remains unavailable (`f_recomputed=NaN`, `f_consistent=false`). The explicit full-threshold objective agrees with the reported objective and independent calculation; both the unavailable backend flag and explicit comparison are retained. The first fresh attempt also exposed an empty-table writer error when no theta endpoints failed. That harness error was fixed, and the same fresh draws were replayed without changing a statistical or optimization setting.\n\n")
  cat("## Reproduce\n\nUse matching isolated-worktree bindings and Python with mpmath 1.3.0; use fresh output IDs. The retained replay reads this leaf's saved `ordinal-audit-confirm-v1/case_9.rds` and original fit objects. Recreate them with the earlier ordinal lane at seed 865051201, two replicates, when local raw artifacts are absent.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --ordinal-audit --sparse-search --retained --run-id sparse-retained-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --ordinal-audit --sparse-search --reps 10 --seed-base 865052301 --run-id sparse-confirm-new --python /path/to/python\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:sparse_search -P sparse_run:sparse-confirm-new -P sparse_retained:sparse-retained-new\n```\n\nReopen for a finite accurate theta endpoint that improves on the retained local face, an unexplained failure within the regular finite scope, or implementation of a boundary/PSD audit. Broader starts, FIML patterns, ML2S handoffs, shared stopping behavior and default adoption retain their own cards. Other report lanes remain selectable.\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
}

  cat("\n\nWeights are checked against independent empirical centered-moment covariance and normal-theory formulas. DWLS uses the inverse empirical diagonal; ADF inverts the full empirical matrix. Lower-vech residuals mirror the sample lower triangle. Component tests also exercise native diagonal arithmetic, zero-weight rank loss, negative diagonal rejection and nonlinear mean coordinates.\n\n### Fresh fitting confirmation\n\nTwo new datasets per family use skewed latent scores and N = 120; the second group has N = 180. The regular and mean families cover all weights; ties, identified feedback, groups and mixed units use GLS, DWLS and DLS. The deliberately redundant feedback model is a separate rejection control. All marker fits use advertised complete-data APIs with automatic weight construction; sphere checks use supplied fixed weights for a small subset.\n\n")
  shown <- data.frame(Family=families$family,Chart=families$chart,Fits=families$fits,
    Qualified=families$verified_passed,Failed=families$failed,Unchecked=families$unchecked,
    `Legacy losses`=families$legacy_losses,check.names=FALSE)
  cat(knitr::kable(shown,row.names=FALSE),sep="\n")
  value <- function(k)metadata$value[metadata$key==k]
  cat(sprintf("\n\nThe R generation/fitting/audit/export phase took %.1f seconds and the serial 90-digit reference phase %.1f seconds on this workstation. The times include binding and artifact costs and are not a standalone optimizer benchmark. The complete failed/unchecked endpoint inventory is retained in `failures.csv`.\n\n",
    as.numeric(value("elapsed_s")),reference$elapsed_s[1]))
  cat("## Caveats\n\nThis is a bounded numerical check with actual default starts, PORT-NLS stock controls and sample-unit coordinates. It is not the full no-options fitter, a population reliability estimate, a comparison of starts, or a claim of best-basin recovery. The signed two-factor ULS recipe is not used. Positive local curvature and a small distance do not establish statistical identification or global optimality.\n\nThe supported enclosure conditions on binary64 model, sample, weight and map inputs. Producer recipe checks are separate from propagation of first-stage numerical error. Complete mean blocks and unequal groups are covered; partial mean blocks, ordinal/mixed threshold maps, ML2S handoffs, FIML patterns, PSD faces, boxes and barriers need their own integration or supported bounds. ML remains covariance-only in this interval producer. Supplied singular weights and deficient metrics authorize no pass. Ordinary acceptance defaults are unchanged.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nUse the matching worktree magmaanlab build and Python with mpmath 1.3.0. Choose fresh run IDs; raw samples, matrices and fitted objects remain ignored. Frozen comparison, recipe, failure and summary CSVs preserve the judgments and provenance.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --weighted-audit --smoke --run-id weighted-smoke-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --weighted-audit --run-id weighted-confirm-new --python /path/to/python\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:weighted_audit -P weighted_run:weighted-confirm-new\n```\n\nReopen for a missed enclosure, producer/unit mismatch, unexplained acceptance, or a new moment/domain representation. Ordinal and ML2S can now reuse this mechanism after their own map, producer and handoff checks. Previous lanes, including `uls_search`, remain selectable.\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
} else if (identical(params$lane, "uls_search")) {
  read_search <- function(run,name) {
    path <- file.path("results",run,paste0(name,".csv"))
    if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing search evidence: ",path,
      "; run --ordinary --uls-search, scripts/uls_search_basins.py and scripts/verify_uls_search.py")
    read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }
  runs <- c(params$search_retained_stock,params$search_retained_tight,params$search_stock,params$search_tight)
  stock <- read_search(params$search_stock,"family_summary")
  tight <- read_search(params$search_tight,"family_summary")
  retained <- read_search(params$search_retained_stock,"family_summary")
  retained_tight <- read_search(params$search_retained_tight,"family_summary")
  v <- do.call(rbind,lapply(runs,read_search,name="verification"))
  cat("## Question\n\nCan sample-only starts repair the retained weak-marker and mixed-unit ULS search failures, with PORT-NLS, sample-unit scaling and the verified Newton audit held fixed? Does tightening optimizer controls add anything?\n\n")
  cat("## Short answer\n\nOn 30 fresh draws, the native sphere route with its default start plus four signed moment starts qualifies all 10 regular, 10 weak-marker and 10 mixed-unit fits. Every selected endpoint matches the best independently refined local minimum found. The marker portfolio qualifies 10, 6 and 8 respectively; tighter controls raise its mixed-unit count to 10 but leave weak markers at 6, at substantially greater cost. No default-start success is lost by retaining the default in the portfolio.\n\nThis is unrestricted, covariance-only ULS: some winners have negative residual variances or indefinite latent covariances. The four signed starts are specific to this two-factor design. These results establish a useful experimental search recipe, with local accuracy checks; they do not settle software defaults, PSD-constrained fitting or global optimality.\n\n")
  cat("## Evidence\n\n### Starts help; tight controls mainly help mixed-unit marker fits\n\nEach fresh family contains ten N = 100 sampled datasets. Thirteen cold fits per dataset compare the actual API start, a shared default physical start for sphere, layered/native starts and four signed moment starts in both charts. All constructed starts use only that dataset's moments and are constructed before fitting. The five-call portfolio selects the lowest original objective among endpoints passing objective consistency and the opt-in Newton audit. Its entire verified distance interval must lie within 0.01 and its observed curvature must be positive.\n\n")
  shown <- stock[stock$portfolio=="default_signed",]
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(shown)),function(i) {
    z <- shown[i,]; b <- stock[stock$family==z$family & stock$chart==z$chart & stock$portfolio=="api_default",]
    t <- tight[tight$family==z$family & tight$chart==z$chart & tight$portfolio=="default_signed",]
    data.frame(Family=c(regular="Regular",weak="Weak markers",mixed="Mixed units")[[z$family]],Chart=z$chart,
      `Default start`=paste0(b$qualified," / 10"),`Default + signed`=paste0(z$qualified," / 10"),
      `Tight + signed`=paste0(t$qualified," / 10"),`Stock portfolio (ms)`=round(1000*z$median_seconds),
      `Tight portfolio (ms)`=round(1000*t$median_seconds),check.names=FALSE)
  })
  cat(knitr::kable(do.call(rbind,rows),row.names=FALSE),sep="\n")
  cat("\n\nTimes are medians for all five calls, including their audits and binding overhead. They are short workstation timings, not a benchmark of audit overhead alone. All qualified portfolio winners in this table also match the best known local reference objective within 1e-6 × (1 + |F|).\n\n")
  cat("Here 'default start' means default-start PORT-NLS: no start override is supplied to the API, while the optimizer and scaling are explicitly fixed. It is not the full no-options ordinary fitter, whose optimizer is L-BFGS. The marker ULS start is FABIN3/native, not the layered start used in the preceding audit-integration study. Native sphere uses its canonical start; a separate shared-default arm controls the physical input. Returned start vectors are checked against the requested/default pre-chart input.\n\nStock controls retain route-specific iteration budgets (marker 1,000; sphere 2,000). Tight controls set both to 10,000, evaluations to 100,000, relative objective tolerance to 1e-14 and absolute objective, step and false-convergence tolerances to zero. Start comparisons hold controls fixed within each route; the stock budgets are not identical across charts. A zero PORT evaluation count is an uninstrumented sentinel and is not used as a work measurement.\n\n")
  cat("### Retained failures are search failures\n\nThe ten retained datasets contain five weak-marker and five mixed-unit cases from the previous terminal study. At its layered starts, weak-marker marker fits include two nonpositive-curvature endpoints and one positive-curvature endpoint above budget, all exhausting 1,000 iterations. The sphere has two above-budget endpoints after singular-convergence stops. All five mixed-unit layered marker fits have nonpositive curvature and exhaust their budget; two sphere endpoints exhaust theirs and remain uncertified, with independent distances above budget. These are not accurate minima incorrectly rejected by the audit.\n\nAgainst actual default starts on those retained datasets, the stock default-plus-signed portfolio raises weak-marker qualifications from 2/5 to 4/5 in marker and 3/5 to 5/5 in sphere. Mixed units rise from 0/5 to 2/5 in marker and 3/5 to 5/5 in sphere. Tightening raises the mixed-unit marker portfolio to 5/5 but leaves weak markers at 4/5. Fresh confirmation therefore repeats the main distinction: signed starts plus the native sphere route succeed where marker coordinates and extra iterations alone still leave gaps.\n\nDropping the default start loses one retained weak-marker marker success and one fresh weak-marker marker success: none of the four signed starts qualifies in those cases. Keeping the default avoids both losses. Every qualification loss and worse-objective loss is retained in each run's `losses.csv`; the default-plus-signed portfolio has neither kind of loss against the stock default-start baseline.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("### Independent numerical checks\n\nAcross retained and fresh runs, %d cold fits produce %d selected endpoint reference checks. The independent 90-digit calculation checks API-default endpoints, layered controls, qualified portfolio winners and lowest finite endpoints; it does not check every raw fit. All %d available construction-bound checks, curvature margins and finite distance intervals cover, with no wrong decisive classification or original-objective discrepancy. Numerical qualification and agreement with a better local basin are retained separately.\n\n",sum(v$fits),sum(v$reference_points),sum(v$available_bound_checks)))
  cat("Independent basin refinement profiles diagonal residual variances out of the original ULS objective and uses seven free loading-ratio/latent-covariance coordinates. Seeds are selected only after all cold fits finish; they are never supplied to those fits. A reference requires a stationary profiled point and positive equilibrated analytic profile curvature. The endpoint checks independently assess full-model observed curvature. The best refined objective supplies a local comparison, not a proof that all basins have been found.\n\nThe first reference refinement requested a 75-digit scaled-score residual at 90-digit working precision. It produced references for all ten retained cases but only 27/30 stock and 28/30 tight fresh cases; its failed attempts and timings are preserved. After observing these failures, the reference-only protocol was amended to request 40 digits, still working at 90 digits. Chasing a 75-digit score can require objective decreases below the working precision, stalling the line search. The 40-digit repeat provides references for every case and is ample for the 1e-6 objective comparison. This amendment changes neither cold fits nor the 0.01 endpoint audit budget.\n\n")
  cat("## Caveats\n\nThe target deliberately imposes neither positive residual variances nor PSD constraints. Among the ten sphere portfolio winners per fresh family, negative residual variances occur in 1 regular, 3 weak-marker and 7 mixed-unit cases; indefinite latent covariances occur in 0, 5 and 1 respectively. These counts overlap. They are numerical ULS successes under the stated unrestricted target, not admissible constrained SEM solutions.\n\nTen draws per family cannot establish a population success rate. The signed starts exploit this model's two three-indicator factors and structural-regression representation; they are not yet a general SEM start policy. Tied labels, feedback, groups, means, other LS weights, ML, FIML, ordinal data, active boxes, PSD faces and barriers need their own evidence. Sphere chart availability remains distinct from native endpoint qualification. No regularization is introduced, and no library/binding implementation or default changes in this lane.\n\n")
  meta_value <- function(run,key) {z<-read_search(run,"metadata");as.numeric(z$value[z$key==key])}
  timing <- lapply(c(params$search_stock,params$search_tight),function(run) {
    c(fits=meta_value(run,"fit_elapsed_s"),endpoints=read_search(run,"reference_metadata")$elapsed_s,
      basin75=read_search(run,"basin_metadata")$elapsed_s,basin40=read_search(run,"basin-40/basin_metadata")$elapsed_s)
  })
  cat(sprintf("Fresh stock/tight fitting and artifact collection took %.1f/%.1f seconds; selected endpoint checking took %.1f/%.1f seconds. Independent basin refinement took %.1f/%.1f seconds at the original residual target and %.1f/%.1f seconds at the amended target. Jobs used one math thread under nice 10. Raw fit objects, sample matrices and pilots remain local; compact judgments, losses, failed reference attempts and provenance are frozen.\n\n",timing[[1]][1],timing[[2]][1],timing[[1]][2],timing[[2]][2],timing[[1]][3],timing[[2]][3],timing[[1]][4],timing[[2]][4]))
  cat("The next implementation question is how to construct and price bounded sample-only portfolios for broader SEM models. Default adoption requires a separate prespecified decision study with the full actual-default fitter, held-out models, every loss and explicit runtime criteria. Accurate-but-uncertified weak-marker ML remains a separate audit task.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nUse the matching magmaanlab build and Python with mpmath 1.3.0; choose fresh IDs. The retained phase reads this leaf's local `audit-terminal-final-v1` samples, regenerated by the preceding `--audit-terminal` lane if absent. The fresh phase is independent of them. The example below regenerates fresh evidence. Regenerate both retained phases and their references/verifications in the same way to rebuild every panel on a clean checkout; otherwise the frozen retained summaries supply those panels. Use the same seed base for stock/tight pairing.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --uls-search --phase fresh --smoke --run-id search-smoke-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --uls-search --phase retained --controls stock --run-id retained-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --uls-search --phase fresh --controls stock --run-id stock-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --uls-search --phase fresh --controls tight --run-id tight-new --python /path/to/python\nnice -n 10 /path/to/python scripts/uls_search_basins.py --run-dir results/stock-new\nnice -n 10 /path/to/python scripts/uls_search_basins.py --run-dir results/stock-new --score-digits 40 --output-subdir basin-40\nnice -n 10 /path/to/python scripts/uls_search_basins.py --run-dir results/tight-new\nnice -n 10 /path/to/python scripts/uls_search_basins.py --run-dir results/tight-new --score-digits 40 --output-subdir basin-40\npython3 scripts/verify_uls_search.py --run-dir results/stock-new --basin-subdir basin-40\npython3 scripts/verify_uls_search.py --run-dir results/tight-new --basin-subdir basin-40 --baseline-run results/stock-new\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:uls_search -P search_stock:stock-new -P search_tight:tight-new\n```\n\nPrevious lanes, including `audit_terminal`, remain selectable.\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
} else if (identical(params$lane, "audit_terminal")) {
  read_terminal <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path("results",params$terminal_run,paste0(name,".csv"))
    if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing terminal evidence: ",path,"; run --ordinary --audit-terminal and scripts/verify_audit_terminal.py")
    read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }
  v <- read_terminal("verification"); families <- read_terminal("family_summary")
  points <- read_terminal("comparisons"); losses <- read_terminal("losses")
  timing <- read_terminal("reference_metadata"); metadata <- read_terminal("metadata")
  endpoints <- points[points$target==0,]
  cat("## Question\n\nCan construction-aware ULS and complete-data normal-theory ML audits qualify actual optimizer endpoints in ordinary and sphere coordinates, while retaining objective, feasibility and curvature failures?\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("## Short answer\n\nThe opt-in terminal assessment is implemented, including the sphere normalization and its full second-derivative chain. Across %d sampled problems and %d endpoint/perturbation checks, every available construction bound and distance interval agrees with the independent 90-digit reference; no decisive classification is wrong. Of %d optimizer endpoints, %d pass, %d fail and %d remain unresolved. Failed endpoints have nonpositive curvature or exceed the accuracy budget; unresolved arithmetic stays visible. This numerical confirmation changes no library default.\n\n",v$cases,v$points,v$endpoints,v$endpoint_passes,v$endpoint_failures,v$endpoint_unresolved))
  cat("## Evidence\n\nEach family has five new sampled covariance datasets. Marker and sphere routes start from the same sample-only layered/native physical point; ULS uses PORT-NLS and ML uses PORT, with sample-unit scaling and no sphere polish. The cases cover regular and weak markers, mixed measurement units, tied loading labels, fixed feedback, and two unequal-sized groups. This is a controlled search recipe rather than a default-comparison study.\n\n")
  pretty <- c(regular="Regular",weak="Weak markers",mixed="Mixed units",shared="Tied loadings",feedback="Feedback",groups="Two groups")
  routes <- expand.grid(chart=c("marker","sphere"),estimator=c("ULS","ML"),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  table <- data.frame(Family=unname(pretty[unique(families$family)]),check.names=FALSE)
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(routes))) {
    z <- families[families$chart==routes$chart[k] & families$estimator==routes$estimator[k],]
    table[[paste(routes$estimator[k],routes$chart[k],"passes")]] <- paste(z$selected_passes,z$calls,sep=" / ")
  }
  cat(knitr::kable(table,row.names=FALSE),sep="\n")
  cat(sprintf("\n\nAll %d available construction bounds enclose the measured matrix, score and curvature errors; their verified positive-curvature lower bounds are conservative. The %d within-budget and %d above-budget decisions are correct, with %d unresolved intervals. The marker perturbations add %d points by increasing one residual variance by 1%% or 5%% of its sample variance; %d pass the selected terminal assessment. These are numerical challenge controls, separate from endpoint success.\n\n",v$available,v$within,v$above,v$unresolved,v$perturbed_controls,v$control_passes))
  cat("The 11 failed endpoints comprise eight independently nonpositive observed curvatures and three positive-curvature endpoints above budget. The three unchecked endpoints are one weak-marker sphere ML point whose exact local distance is 0.000429, and two mixed-unit sphere ULS points whose exact distances are 0.697 and 0.514. Thus one accurate endpoint is withheld by the conservative arithmetic check, while two inaccurate endpoints remain uncertified. Of the 27 unresolved distance intervals, 24 retain nonpositive-curvature failures; they are not unchecked terminal verdicts.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("### Changed verdicts\n\nAt the same endpoints, the opt-in assessment gains %d passes over the original audit and loses %d. Every loss is retained in `losses.csv`, including its family, estimator, chart and high-precision distance. Both verdicts remain available. A within-budget distance alone cannot override failed feasibility or objective consistency.\n\n",sum(families$gains),v$losses))
  if (nrow(losses)) {
    shown <- losses[c("family","case_id","estimator","chart","reference_distance","decision","selected_status")]
    names(shown) <- c("Family","Case","Estimator","Chart","Reference distance","Interval decision","Selected status")
    cat(knitr::kable(shown,row.names=FALSE,digits=4),sep="\n")
    cat("\n\n")
  }
  cat("### What is assessed\n\nThe ordinary reusable terminal report independently encloses model moments, analytic observed curvature and the sampling metric. The sphere producer additionally reconstructs the exact retained binary64 map, including loading radii, the Jacobian, the second-derivative contraction with the full physical score, and transport into the retained tangent/QR coordinates. It bounds the local diagnostic at this point, rather than distance to an actual optimum.\n\nThe opt-in policy requires the entire verified interval to lie within 0.01, plus finite original objective, consistency and feasibility. Nonpositive observed curvature fails; unresolved rank, missing bounds or an interval crossing the budget supplies no pass. Neither ridge regularization nor a truncated inverse is used. `evaluate_at(..., audit_options=list(verified_newton=TRUE))` selects the ordinary explicit point assessment; a backend objective can be supplied for endpoint consistency checking. `frontier_fit_sphere(..., control=list(verified_newton=TRUE))` selects the native endpoint assessment before chart translation/polish. Missing evidence is represented by NA, with the original verdict retained separately.\n\n")
  costs <- aggregate(total_fit_audit_seconds~family,families,sum)
  cat(sprintf("## Caveats\n\nFive datasets per family can confirm numerical behavior at these retained points, but cannot establish reliable population success rates, identify all basins or settle optimizer/start defaults. The recipe was held fixed after the pilot and uses a distinct sampled seed base. Shared-label and multi-group coverage here does not establish exact nullspace accuracy: retained binary64 bases define the audited numerical coordinates. Means, FIML, other LS weights, active boxes, PSD faces and barriers remain separate extensions. ULS does not require a positive-definite model covariance, while ML does.\n\nThe fit-and-evaluation stage took %.1f seconds and the independent 90-digit stage %.1f seconds, using one math thread under nice 10. Family totals for fitting plus auditing range from %.2f to %.2f seconds; the opt-in audit cost has not been separated from search and binding overhead. These timings support a practical prototype, not a scaling claim. Raw samples, matrices, failed pilots and per-fit rows remain local; compact judgments, every loss and provenance are frozen.\n\n",as.numeric(metadata$value[metadata$key=="evaluation_elapsed_s"]),timing$elapsed_s,min(costs$total_fit_audit_seconds),max(costs$total_fit_audit_seconds)))
  cat("The next decision is whether and where to adopt this assessment by default, with declared criteria, an actual-default baseline and new held-out fitting problems. Starts, basin selection and PORT-NLS original-objective inconsistencies keep separate tasks. The present result completes opt-in audit integration and sampled numerical confirmation, not the whole ULS programme.\n\n## Reproduce\n\nUse the matching magmaanlab build and Python with mpmath 1.3.0, choosing fresh run IDs.\n\n```sh\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --audit-terminal --smoke --run-id terminal-smoke-new --python /path/to/python\nOMP_NUM_THREADS=1 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 nice -n 10 Rscript run_experiment.R --ordinary --audit-terminal --run-id terminal-new --python /path/to/python\npython3 scripts/verify_audit_terminal.py --run-dir results/terminal-new\nquarto render report.qmd -P lane:audit_terminal -P terminal_run:terminal-new\n```\n\n")
  knitr::knit_exit()
} else if (identical(params$lane, "audit_construction")) {
  read_construction <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path("results",params$construction_run,paste0(name,".csv"))
    if (!file.exists(path)) stop("Missing construction evidence: ",path,"; run --ordinary --audit-uncertainty --derive-input-errors and scripts/verify_audit_uncertainty.py")
    read.csv(path,stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  }
  v <- read_construction("verification"); points <- read_construction("comparisons")
  timing <- read_construction("reference_metadata"); metadata <- read_construction("metadata")
  flat <- points[points$role=="retained_NTML" & points$source_case==4 & points$target==0,]
  intervals <- read_construction("intervals")
  flat_interval <- intervals[intervals$role=="retained_NTML" & intervals$source_case==4 & intervals$target==0,]
  cat("## Question\n\nCan the fitting library calculate usable construction-error bounds for ordinary ULS and complete-data normal-theory ML, and distinguish numerical accuracy from unresolved arithmetic without regularizing the objective?\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("## Short answer\n\nYes, for the covariance-only unboxed ambient models tested here. Independently constructed interval bounds qualify all %d numerical minima, including all 25 retained ULS minima and the flat NTML witness. Across %d points, %d decisions agree with the independent 90-digit reference; %d remain unresolved. Every available construction bound and positive-curvature lower bound passes its independent check. The production fit guard is unchanged: this is the earlier fixed-point mechanism check; opt-in integration and sampled confirmation are reported in the audit_terminal lane.\n\n",sum(v$derived_minima_within),sum(v$points),sum(v$derived_within+v$derived_above),sum(v$derived_unresolved)))
  cat("## Evidence\n\nSeven points per case cover 25 retained ULS datasets, 15 fresh exact-population ULS controls and seven retained finite NTML witnesses. The fresh controls comprise five regular, five weak-marker and five mixed-unit populations; their sample matrices are constructed moments. No optimizer is called. ULS perturbations target distances 0, 0.009, 0.00999, 0.01, 0.01001, 0.011 and 0.02; NTML uses variance perturbations that also expose nonpositive curvature.\n\n")
  labels <- c(fresh_mixed_units="Fresh mixed units",fresh_regular="Fresh regular",fresh_weak="Fresh weak markers",retained_NTML="Retained NTML",retained_ULS="Retained ULS")
  table <- data.frame(Controls=unname(labels[v$role]),`Within budget`=v$derived_within,
    `Above budget`=v$derived_above,Unresolved=v$derived_unresolved,
    `Minima within / cases`=paste(v$derived_minima_within,v$cases,sep=" / "),
    `Production passes`=v$actual_passes,check.names=FALSE)
  cat(knitr::kable(table,row.names=FALSE),sep="\n")
  cat(sprintf("\n\nConstruction bounds are available for %d points; all measured matrix, score and curvature errors lie inside them, and all positive-curvature lower bounds are conservative. The other 15 points have independently nonpositive NTML curvature and retain that failure status. Of the 79 unresolved distances, 40 are nominal ULS threshold points, 24 are nearby retained ULS controls whose intervals still cross the budget, and 15 are the nonpositive-curvature points. There are no wrong decisive interval classifications or missed finite reference distances.\n\n",sum(v$derived_available)))
  cat(sprintf("The flat NTML minimum has independent local distance %.2g. The producer proves a positive equilibrated curvature lower bound of %.2g and returns a distance interval [0, %.2g], well inside 0.01. Its production audit still reports ill conditioned. The earlier dimensional construction allowance left this point unresolved.\n\n",flat$reference_distance,flat$derived_curvature_lower_bound,flat_interval$derived_upper))
  cat(sprintf("### Differences from production acceptance\n\nThe derived interval qualifies %d points that the current production guard rejects: 63 retained ULS points, 15 fresh mixed-unit points and two NTML points. Six production passes on nominal ULS threshold controls become unresolved. One of those six has independent distance 0.010000000000000152, just above the binary64 budget; the interval correctly withholds a decision. There are no production passes classified decisively above budget by the new interval. Every point and disagreement is retained in comparisons.csv; this run changes no fitting default.\n\n",sum(v$derived_within_actual_failed)))
  cat("### How the bounds are constructed\n\nThe C++ producer treats the supplied binary64 point, sample matrices, fixed structural cells and retained coordinate maps as exact inputs. It recomputes the SEM moments and analytic first and second derivatives with outward long-double intervals. Each scalar operation expands by one representable value in each direction; uncertain pivots, nonfinite enclosures and unproved positive definiteness stay unresolved. Repeated parameter labels, linear equality reductions and cell overwrites follow the model contract. Owning tests also exercise a feedback model and unequal-sized groups.\n\n")
  cat("For ULS, interval sample Cholesky roots construct the sampling factor and whitened residual independently. The producer compares those targets with the retained scaled artifacts. It assembles observed curvature in the actual QR coordinates, forming the Gauss-Newton term after applying the coordinate map and adding the independent second-derivative correction. For NTML it recomputes the implied covariance inverse, total score and full observed Hessian in the retained equilibrated coordinates. A verified triangular inverse supplies a lower bound for positive curvature; no ridge or truncated inverse is used.\n\n")
  cat("The distance kernels then include retained factorization defects, projection or solve arithmetic, and the calculated construction bounds. Within budget means the entire numerical interval is at most 0.01; above budget means the entire interval exceeds it. An interval crossing the budget, uncertain rank or uncertain positive curvature supplies no pass. This bounds the local diagnostic at the supplied point; it does not bound distance to an actual optimum or establish global optimality. The earlier assumed dimensional allowance remains available as the audit_uncertainty lane.\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("## Caveats\n\nThis is fixed-point numerical validation, not sampled fitting confirmation. The producer supports covariance-only single-level ULS and complete-data ML in unboxed ambient geometry. Means, native sphere normalization, other LS weight systems, PSD faces and barriers require separate extensions. Numerical controls remain separate from statistical identification and from optimizer/start selection. Standard floating-point rounding, correctly rounded basic operations and square roots, and gradual underflow are part of the arithmetic contract.\n\nThe %d-point R evaluation took %.1f seconds, including retained and dimensional-sensitivity artifacts; the independent 90-digit check took %.1f seconds. Both used one math thread under nice 10. Optional evaluate_at artifacts leave the stored verdict intact. All 568 optimized C++ estimate tests (14,314 assertions) and 104 sphere R assertions pass. Raw matrices remain local; compact judgments and fingerprints are frozen.\n\n",sum(v$points),as.numeric(metadata$value[metadata$key=="evaluation_elapsed_s"]),timing$elapsed_s))
  cat("Opt-in terminal integration, sphere transport and fresh sampled/model-family confirmation are now reported in the audit_terminal lane. Default adoption remains separate. } else if (identical(params$lane, "audit_uncertainty")) {
